subject: Changing prior has no effect on result

messages.author: bafbff7f5abd72d1
messages.subject: Changing prior has no effect on result
parts:
I am worried that I have not been specifying my models correctly.

I try two different priors:

priortest1<-c(set_prior("cauchy(0, 2.5)",class = "b", coef = "IV"),set_prior("cauchy(0, 10)", class = "Intercept", coef = ""))
priortest2<-c(set_prior("cauchy(10000, 2.5)",class = "b", coef = "IV"),set_prior("cauchy(0, 10)", class = "Intercept", coef = ""))

And implement them in the following two models:

1test<-brm(DV~IV+(1|Subject), data = data, family="gaussian", prior = priortest1, warmup = 1000, iter = 2000, chains = 20, save_all_pars = TRUE, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9))
2test<-brm(DV~IV+(1|Subject), data = data, family="gaussian", prior = priortest2, warmup = 1000, iter = 2000, chains = 20, save_all_pars = TRUE, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9))

However the coefficient on IV is nearly identical in each case; for 1test:

Population-Level Effects: 
          Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Eff.Sample Rhat
Intercept     3.23      0.25     2.73     3.71      20000 1.00
Tongue       -0.20      0.46    -1.11     0.72      20000 1.00 

For 2test:

Population-Level Effects: 
          Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Eff.Sample Rhat
Intercept     3.23      0.24     2.75     3.70      20000 1.00
Tongue       -0.21      0.48    -1.13     0.74      20000 1.00

Is this simply a matter of the likelihood dominating the prior?
